entry.title: AI-Powered Real-Time Egyptian Sign Language Translator
entry.summary: I recently worked on a project focused on accessibility and AI: a real-time Egyptian Sign Language (ESL) translator designed to help reduce communication barriers for the Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing community in Egypt. The system uses computer vision and deep learning to recognize continuous sign language sequences in real time. Instead of focusing on isolated characters, the model processes temporal gesture sequences, allowing more natural translation. Key components include: ** MediaPipe-based holistic keypoint extraction A sequence model (BiLSTM) for gesture understanding Context-aware post-processing to merge letters into meaningful words Optional text-to-speech for accessibility ** The goal is not just technical accuracy, but practical usability on standard hardware with low latency. I wrote a detailed article explaining the motivation, architecture, and challenges here: 👉 Full article on Medium: https://ahmedashrafmo.medium.com/real-time-egyptian-sign-language-translator-ai-powered-solution-to-empower-the-deaf-community-in-727430624b1c I’d really appreciate feedback from people working in AI, accessibility, or sign language technology.

entry.title: Learning Programming as Paying Debt, Not Investment
entry.summary:
It is the end of 2025.
More than two years have passed since I started learning programming on my own through the internet. And like the years before, I still feel as if I have made no real progress. Why does it feel that way? I think the answer is simple: for a long time, I did not have a clear unease—no concrete reason for what I wanted to do with programming itself. So I want to trace this back.
Why did I choose to learn programming in the first place? When I was a child, I experienced something close to existential anxiety.
